Magalona]] | [[Murcia, Negros Occidental|Murcia]] }} | year = 1907 | members_label = Representative | members = [[Javi Benitez]] | blank1_name = Political party | blank1_info = {{Color box|{{party color|Partido Federal ng Pilipinas}}|border=darkgray}} [[Partido Federal ng Pilipinas|PFP]] | blank2_name = Congressional bloc | blank2_info = Majority }} '''Negros Occidental's 3rd congressional district''' is one of the six [[congressional districts of the Philippines]] in the province of [[Negros Occidental]]. It has been represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] since 1916 and earlier in the [[Philippine Assembly]] from 1907 to 1916.{{cite web|url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/legislators/?v=province |title=Roster of Philippine legislators |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |accessdate=April 23, 2020}} The district consists of the cities of [[Silay]], [[Talisay, Negros Occidental|Talisay]] and [[Victorias]], as well as the adjacent municipalities of [[Enrique B. Magalona, Negros Occidental|Enrique B. Magalona]] and [[Murcia, Negros Occidental|Murcia]]. The seat is currently represented in the [[20th Congress of the Philippines|20th Congress]] by [[Javi Benitez|Javier Miguel L. Benitez]] of the [[Partido Federal ng Pilipinas]] (PFP). The district served as an electoral district in the [[Philippine Constitutional Convention of 1934|1934 Constitutional Convention]], electing two delegates, and in the [[Philippine Constitutional Convention of 1971|1971 Constitutional Convention]], electing four delegates.{{Cite PH act|url=https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/28/15525|chamber=Act|number=4125|date=May 26, 1934|title=An Act to Provide for the Election and Holding of the Constitutional Convention Authorized by the Act of the Congress of the United States of March Twenty-Fourth, Nineteen Hundred and Thirty-Four, Appropriate Funds Therefor, and for Other Purposes}}{{Cite PH act|url=https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/14108|chamber=RA|number=6132|date=August 24, 1970|title=An Act Implementing Resolution of Both Houses Numbered Two as Amended by Resolution of Both Houses Numbered Four of the Congress of the Philippines Calling for a Constitutional Convention, Providing for Proportional Representation Therein and Other Details Relating to the Election of Delegates to and the Holding of the Constitutional Convention, Repealing for the Purpose Republic Act Four Thousand Nine Hundred Fourteen, and for Other Purposes}} It is one of two congressional districts that produced at least two House Speakers (the other district is [[Leyte's 1st congressional district|Leyte's 1st]]): [[Gil Montilla]] and [[José Yulo]]. {{clear}} == List of members representing the district == === Philippine Assembly (1907–1916) === {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center" ! width="100px" | Portrait ! width="135px" | Member
